kind_note: research prototype: a reinforcement learning system trained to find kissing-number configurations, not an agent harness
note: Kind and lab corrected. The kind 'harness' is wrong. The arXiv paper 'Finding Kissing Numbers with Game-theoretic Reinforcement Learning' (arXiv 2511.13391) describes the system as 'a reinforcement learning system, PackingStar, to solve it', applied to the kissing number problem as a cooperative matrix-completion game. It is a research system, not shipped software. Lab: the 'Ma et al.' attribution fits first author Chengdong Ma; affiliations listed include Peking University's Institute for Artificial Intelligence, the Shanghai Academy of AI for Science, and Fudan University. The v1 submission date (17 Nov 2025) is a paper date, not a public-availability date, so it is not used as a release date. No sentence in the paper, and no GitHub repository, model release, or press report I found, says PackingStar was made publicly available for use. The 'agent harness' search returned an unrelated Peking University item, Harness-Zero, which I could not confirm has the same authors; it was not used. If a public code or model release is later found, revisit release_basis.
